subject: Commit sculpting: MAP milestones, TPM targets, and evaluation gates
messages:
From: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@atlas-retail.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@atlas-retail.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@atlas-retail.com>
Date: 2026-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff follow-up — proposed MAP and evaluation plan

Thanks for the kickoff this morning, Hannah. The Atlas product team liked the short pilot scope — focusing on checkout fraud detection and personalized search boosting.

Before we lock the pilot, two asks from procurement:
- We need clear monthly token (TPM) targets tied to each MAP milestone so finance can model spend.
- Discounts should be milestone-driven (e.g., percentage credit upon hitting latency/throughput gates).

Can you send a version of the MAP that shows the TPM schedule across the 3-month pilot and the discount ladder? Also please include the sample eval dataset you mentioned so our SREs can sanity-check performance.

Best,
Alex

--
Alex Reynolds
Director, Engineering — Atlas Retail
alex.reynolds@atlas-retail.com
+1 (415) 555-0126
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@atlas-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-09T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff follow-up — proposed MAP and evaluation plan

Alex — thanks for the quick note. Attaching a draft MAP and evaluation matrix per your asks (MAP_v1_Atlas_Retail.pdf, evaluation_plan_matrix.csv). Key points up front:

- Pilot length: 12 weeks (3 months) with 4 internal milestones (Week 2, 4, 8, 12).
- TPM schedule (monthly): Month 1 = 1.2M tokens, Month 2 = 3.5M tokens, Month 3 = 6M tokens. These are starting targets we can sculpt.
- Discount ladder: 5% credit at Milestone 2 (stable latency under 200ms P95), 10% at Milestone 3 (throughput sustained at agreed TPM for 72h), 15% at Milestone 4 (production acceptance). Credits applied to Month 3 invoice as a one-time back-credit.

Notes/risks: if Atlas needs a faster ramp, we can add burst capacity but that changes unit pricing; similarly, smaller initial TPMs can be accepted in exchange for a steeper ramp and lower initial commit.

Next steps I propose: Ben to review pricing terms and suggest a counter-proposal if Atlas needs different tiering; Laura to coordinate procurement redlines.

Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-10T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: suggested adjustments to Atlas MAP (pricing/TPM)

Hannah/Laura — quick internal note after reviewing Alex's asks and the draft MAP. My suggested changes to make the commercials more flexible while protecting unit economics:

1) Smooth ramping: instead of the sharp Month 1/2/3 numbers, propose Month 1 = 800k, Month 2 = 2.5M, Month 3 = 6M. Rationale: lowers early exposure while preserving final commit.
2) Milestone discounts: keep the same ladder but change application to 'future invoicing' (not back-credit) — that avoids cash flow hits.
3) Add a soft-fallback clause: if sustained TPM for 72h is missed due to customer load patterns, allow a single 30-day remediation window before credit triggers.
4) Provide an engineering sample: include a lightweight eval harness and the 10k-record sample set (attached).

I can draft the counter proposal language. Also recommend looping in Prio (Priyom) for sequencing and acceptance criteria — he can own the technical acceptance checklist.

-Ben

--
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@atlas-retail.com>, Procurement <procurement@atlas-retail.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@atlas-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-12T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff follow-up — proposed MAP and evaluation plan

Alex — appreciate the clear asks. Per internal review we've updated the MAP to reflect a 'sculpted commit' approach (attached updated MAP_v1_Atlas_Retail.pdf). Highlights: 

- Agreed TPM schedule (sculpted): Month 1 = 800,000 tokens; Month 2 = 2,500,000 tokens; Month 3 = 6,000,000 tokens.
- Discount ladder: 5% future invoice credit at Milestone 2; 10% at Milestone 3; 15% at final acceptance. Credits applied to Month 4 invoice to simplify reconciliation.
- Acceptance and remediation: 72h sustained throughput requirement with a single 30-day remediation window before credits apply.
- Evaluation artifacts: evaluation_plan_matrix.csv and example harness included. Ben will share the lightweight benchmark script; Priyom will own technical acceptance checklist.

Can you confirm the sculpted TPM schedule and the credit application method? If procurement signs off on those two items I will have Laura circulate a concise pricing terms draft (pricing_terms_draft.docx) for redline. Target to finalize commercials and DocuSign signature by 2026-05-20 to keep the pilot start as planned.

Thanks,
Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (650) 555-0199
